transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having trouble staying with things, attention-wise. Like at work, I can start a safety briefing or go through a plan review really trying to focus, and then a few minutes in my mind’s already jumped to three other job problems. Then I realize I missed something I should’ve caught.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… it’s been enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it. Does that make sense?

Have you had trouble with attention like this for a long time, or is this something that started more recently? Also, does this happen just at work or in other parts of your life too, like at home or during leisure activities?

It’s not brand-new, no. I mean, I’ve probably always had some of it, but the part where it’s really been messing with my job has been… about two years, maybe a little over. Two years and a couple months, I’d say.

It got a lot more noticeable after our construction schedule changed and the hours got more chaotic. Since then it’s been harder to keep things straight. I don’t know if that’s the kind of timeline you’re asking for.
Do you also notice these attention problems in other parts of your life, like at home, while driving, or during hobbies?

Yeah… I mean, the clearest place I notice it is still at work. Like I can start a safety briefing or a plan review really trying to pay attention, and within a few minutes my mind is off on three other job problems. Then I’ll realize I missed something I know I should’ve caught.

At home or hobbies, I guess it’s harder for me to say for sure… but the work part is definitely what made me come in. Is that answering what you mean?
Outside of work, do you find it hard to focus or stay attentive during everyday tasks or hobbies, like when you're at home or trying to relax?

I guess outside work it’s… a little harder for me to pin down, honestly. The main thing I keep noticing is at work—like I’ll start a safety briefing or a plan review really trying to stay with it, and then within a few minutes my mind is already on three other job problems. Then I realize I missed something I should’ve caught.

So, I’m not trying to dodge your question… it’s just the work stuff is the clearest example for me.
When you're at home, do you find it hard to focus on tasks like chores, reading, or watching TV, or does your mind tend to wander during those times too?

At home… I’m not sure I notice it as clearly, or maybe I just don’t pay as much attention to it there. I don’t want to overstate it.

What really stands out, and what brought me in, is work. I can start a safety briefing or be going over a plan and I’m genuinely trying to listen, but a few minutes in my mind is already off on other job problems. Then I’ll realize I missed something I know I should’ve caught. That’s the part that’s been worrying me.
When you're going through these attention struggles at work, do you also find yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a few days at a time?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I miss things at work, and that can put me in a bad mood for a bit. But I wouldn’t say I’m feeling hopeless or losing interest in things for days at a time.

At least, not that I’ve really noticed. Is that kind of what you’re asking?
Have you had days where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even if just for a short time?

Maybe for a short stretch, yeah, like if I’ve had a rough day and I’m annoyed with myself, I can feel kind of down. But I don’t know that I’d call it losing interest in things I enjoy.

It’s more like frustration that passes, I think. I’m trying to answer that right—I haven’t really noticed it being a bigger pattern than that.
Do you ever feel restless or have a hard time staying still, especially during tasks that require focus, like meetings or paperwork?

Yeah… I guess I do, more than I’d like to admit. In meetings especially, when everyone else is just sitting through it, I’m usually the one who ends up standing up, getting coffee, stepping outside to “check something,” that kind of thing.

I try to make it look like I’m just being useful, not disruptive, but honestly sometimes I just need to move around. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you also feel restless or have a hard time staying still during other tasks that require focus, like when you're doing paperwork or even at home trying to relax?

Yeah, I mean… mostly in those situations where I’m supposed to just sit and focus. Like meetings, I can usually find some reason to get up—grab coffee, step out to check something, walk around a bit.

I don’t think I’m trying to be disruptive or anything. I just get uncomfortable sitting there the whole time when everyone else seems fine with it. Does that make sense?
Do you also find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around when you're at home, like when you're trying to watch TV, read, or relax?

At home… I’m not sure I notice it as much, or maybe it’s just not as obvious. The clearest thing is still meetings, honestly. Like when everyone else can sit through the whole thing, I’m the guy who ends up standing up, going to get coffee, stepping outside to “check something,” or finding some excuse to move around.

I try to keep it looking normal, like I’m just handling something, but yeah… I guess it is that needing-to-move feeling. Is that what you’re getting at?

Do you also find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or feeling the need to get up and move around when you're doing other tasks that require focus, like paperwork or even when you're at home relaxing?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it fidgeting exactly, but the getting up part, yes. Like I said, in meetings where everybody else seems able to sit through the whole thing, I’m usually the one standing up, walking over to get coffee, stepping outside to “check something,” or finding some reason to move around.

I try not to make it obvious or bother anybody, but… yeah, I guess that’s probably what you mean.
Do you find yourself getting up or needing to move around even when you're doing paperwork at work or trying to relax at home, like when reading or watching TV?

Yeah… I guess with paperwork it can happen too, but the most obvious example is still meetings. If everyone else is sitting through it, I’m usually the one who ends up standing, going to get coffee, stepping outside to “check something,” or finding some little reason to move around.

I try to make it look like I’m just being productive, not like I can’t sit still… but yeah, that’s probably fair to say.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with attention or a need to move around when you were a child, or is this something that mainly started in adulthood?

Yeah… no, I don’t think it just started as an adult. I mean, I probably would’ve said I was just a busy kid or maybe not the best student, but looking back, yeah, it was there.

In elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, that I talked out of turn. I’d lose homework, too, and I remember rushing through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do. I don’t want to make it sound like I was trying to be difficult or anything… but yeah, it was happening pretty early.
